content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the properties of Group 1 elements
Explain the trend in reactivity down the group
Write equations for reactions with water and oxygen
Explain observations in terms of electronic structure
(Group 1) are lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, and francium. They are the most reactive metals and must be stored under oil to prevent reaction with air and moisture.
(but Li, Na, K still float on water)
Why does reactivity increase down the group?
Atoms get larger down the group
Outer electron is further from nucleus
Less attraction between nucleus and outer electron
Outer electron is lost more easily
Reaction is faster and more vigorous
Floats, fizzes steadily, moves around, slowly gets smaller
Floats, fizzes vigorously, melts into ball, moves rapidly, may ignite (yellow flame)
Floats, fizzes violently, ignites immediately (lilac flame), may explode, moves erratically
[DIAGRAM: Sodium reacting with water - ball of metal floating, fizzing, moving across surface]
Density less than water (for Li, Na, K)
Prevents contact with air (oxygen) and moisture
Safety screens for K, Rb, Cs
Never dispose of in bin or sink
Describe what you would observe when a small piece of potassium is added to water.
It melts into a silvery ball
It moves rapidly/erratically across the surface
It catches fire with a lilac flame
It may explode at the end
Explain why potassium is more reactive than sodium.
Potassium has more electron shells than sodium (4 vs 3)
The outer electron is further from the nucleus
There is more shielding from inner electrons
The outer electron experiences less attraction to the nucleus
The outer electron is lost more easily in potassium
Write the equation for the reaction of lithium with water and name the products.
Explain why alkali metals are stored under oil.
They react with oxygen in the air (tarnish)
They react with water vapour in the air
Oil creates a barrier between the metal and air/moisture
The metals stay shiny and unreacted
Writing NaOH₂ or similar wrong formulae
Products are MOH (one hydroxide ion per metal)
Forgetting to balance equations (e.g., Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂)
State three physical properties of alkali metals. (3 marks)
Write a balanced equation for the reaction of sodium with water. (2 marks)
Describe and explain the trend in reactivity of Group 1 metals going down the group. (4 marks)
Compare the reactions of lithium and potassium with water. Include observations for each. (4 marks)
